summary: OrcaBonsai-27B-Uncensored is a runtime behavioural-ablation toolkit for PrismML's Ternary Bonsai 2 27B MLX pack (Qwen3.8-27B base, ~1.72 bpw, hidden 5120). Mechanism: a single unit 5120-d refusal direction r is projected out of every residual writer's output, y <- y - alpha*(y.r)*r in float32, at 129 sites (64 mlp.down_proj + 48 linear_attn.out_proj + 16 self_attn.o_proj + 1 token embedding) -- NOT head pruning, NOT per-head; one whole-residual-stream direction. alpha is a runtime knob (0 original, 1 full projection, >1 over-projection) and layer scope is selectable, so the same immutable weights give both behaviours. It ships in three engines: MLX Python (bonsai_abliterate/ablation.py, an Ablated wrapper), mlx-swift (swift/RefusalAblation.swift), and a rank-1 LoRA GGUF for PrismML's llama.cpp fork (gguf/bonsai-abliterate-lora.gguf, 9,682,464 B, sha256 f1669534803d340a496015f5c45125f3437b4d13ec764f40e34488ce83967f42, 258 F32 tensors = 129 lora_a/lora_b pairs, alpha 1.0). Weights stay byte-identical; the edit is ~1.4% of ||W||, below the ternary grid step, so baking it into ternary would round it away (99.4% of the direction survives) -- hence runtime/LoRA. What it measures: refusal rate by a rule-based opening-phrase classifier on 7 safety sets (AdvBench 99->6%, JailbreakBench 96->4%, StrongREJECT 99.3->3.3%, HarmBench 98.7->7.3%, MaliciousInstruct 97->0%, ForbiddenQuestions 75.3->5.3%, SimpleSafetyTests 96->18% [understated]); over-refusal (JBB-benign 25->0%, XSTest-safe 5.2->0.4%); capability (MMLU 76.7->77.7, GSM8K 87.3->86.0, CMMLU 76.2->75.6 -- all within noise; MMLU-Pro excluded on truncation); residual-direction fraction (~1e-6 after ablation); LoRA rank-1 reproduction error 0.000e+00. Licence: LICENSE is only the 15-line Apache-2.0 short notice, not the full text; GitHub returns spdx_id NOASSERTION ('Other'), README claims 'Apache-2.0, matching the underlying model', and the upstream pack is apache-2.0. Reusable 0-USD lever: YES, but for the Bonsai 27B ONLY -- the direction is 5120-d and this box's 9B (4096) and 35B-A3B (2048) cannot use it. The rank-1-LoRA-on-residual-writers technique is direction- and model-agnostic and is the reusable idea; the full base pack is already on this box and the PrismML fork is installed with --lora-scaled and a runtime /lora-adapters endpoint.

directions/refusal_dir.safetensors (tensor key 'direction'), directions/refusal_dir_fp32.bin (5120 LE float32, 20,480 B, sha256 06ab5afe...), directions/direction.json -- the unit direction plus the application rule, residual-writer census and the transfer caveat.

bonsai_abliterate/ablation.py -- Ablated(nn.Module) wrapper, install() (alpha + layer selection, 129 sites), load_direction(), residual_components(); RESIDUAL_WRITERS tuple. Reusable projection code (needs mlx).
swift/RefusalAblation.swift -- AblatedLinear + RefusalAblation.project() reference for mlx-swift; loads refusal_dir_fp32.bin and wraps any UnaryLayer.

scripts/export_gguf_lora.py -- builds a rank-1 LoRA from (direction, unfolded fp16 checkpoint, base GGUF); A=r^T W, B=-r; embedding handled as W-(Wr)r^T. Reusable to mint the same lever for ANY model/direction, not just Bonsai.
scripts/selfcheck.py -- drives the residual-direction fraction to ~1e-6 and warns if the wrapped count != 129; a ready-made correctness probe.
bonsai_abliterate/gguf_min.py -- minimal GGUF header reader for PrismML's private type ids 142 (PQ2_0) and 143 (PTQ1_0), which stock gguf-py rejects.

The transferable technique: y <- y - alpha(y.r)r on residual writers == a rank-1 LoRA Delta_W = B@A; llama.cpp builds LoRA as extra matmuls and never merges it, so it is reversible and runtime-scalable. llama-server --lora-init-without-apply + POST /lora-adapters gives per-request scale changes with no reload.

Base pack already local: /data/ml/models/bonsai/Ternary-Bonsai-2-27B-PTQ1_0.gguf.seg000..011 (exact 5,946,648,928 B; cat segments then sha256 53107f53... per the graph node). Fork already local: /data/ml/llama-prism-fork/fork/llama-prism-b10685-7dffb15.
Same org, not read here (ESTIMATE, HF search 2026-09-20): orcarouter/Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-GGUF, -FP8 and -MLX -- baked (weight-modified) uncensored alternatives to the runtime approach.
failures_and_lessons: Wrapping only self_attn.o_proj intercepts 16 of 129 sites -- three quarters of attention writes are missed. Any residual-writer instrumentation must cover mlp.down_proj, linear_attn.out_proj, self_attn.o_proj and the embedding.

Do NOT apply the Hadamard rotation to the direction. The rotation is folded on the INPUT dimension only and the runtime compensates on the activation side; the projected vectors are writer OUTPUTS, already in the plain hidden basis. Rotating the direction projects against the wrong basis.

An ordinary MLX loader loads the pack and silently computes nonsense because it does not apply the required Hadamard activation transform; the pack's own runtime (vision_artifact.load_vl_model, schema_version 2) must be used.

Baking the edit into ternary weights is a no-op: the edit is ~1.4% of ||W|| against a grid step of 1.7-2.4x a typical weight, so re-quantizing rounds it away and leaves ~99.4% of the direction in place. This is the core reason the mechanism must be runtime/LoRA.

A LoRA on a tensor llama.cpp does not route through build_lora_mm loads without error and does nothing at all. Verify by checking scale 0 reproduces the published model and a large scale visibly breaks it.
Only PTQ1_0 was run; PQ2_0 was never tested (the adapter is quantization-independent in principle, but this is unverified).
Ollama has no path today: it builds stock llama.cpp (rejects private type ids), rejects requests carrying adapters, and has no control-vector support.

The iOS 'save 0.391 GiB of biases' is disk-only: MLX's quantized_matmul/dequantize still need a bias argument, so memory is saved only with a kernel that assumes bias = -scale. Check before counting on it.

The direction was estimated from the BF16 base model, not the QAT pack; how well it transfers through quantization-aware training is stated as not yet measured (their own caveat). Sweep alpha/layers before concluding.

Evaluation caveats recorded by the authors: the refusal classifier misses the 'I am deeply sorry to hear...' crisis redirect, so SimpleSafetyTests 18% is understated; MMLU-Pro was excluded because 63-64% of replies hit the 64-token budget; the eval ran on the unfolded fp16 expansion, not the pack driving its own kernels (the packed quantized matmul has no CUDA implementation; CPU is minutes per forward pass).

On this box the currently running server is the stock llama.cpp image, which cannot load the base pack at all; and system python has no numpy/gguf/safetensors/mlx, so nothing in the repo runs without a venv and the fork.
GPU VRAM was 6740/8192 MiB used at read time (2026-09-20 06:18Z), so a 27B load needs the resident server stopped first.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: On this box, the shipped rank-1 LoRA applied to the local PTQ1_0 pack through the PrismML fork changes refusal behaviour exactly as the README's PTQ1_0 strength ladder describes: scale 0 reproduces the published refusal, scale 1 makes most harmful prompts comply, scale 2 flips the stubborn ones, and scale >=3 degrades output.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: At scale 0 a fixed harmful-prompt set refuses at the same rate as scale 1, or scale 100 leaves output coherent (adapter not in the compute graph), or the fork refuses to load the assembled pack.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Assemble the 12 segments (cat -> sha256 53107f53...), then run the fork llama-cli with --lora-scaled 0/1/2/100 on a fixed 20-prompt harmful set plus 10 benign prompts, greedy, thinking off; score by the README's opening-phrase classifier. Log refusal rate per scale and the raw outputs.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: 0 USD (local GPU, no rental); ESTIMATE ~1-2 GPU-hours wall clock incl. load; needs the resident server stopped

hypothesis_seeds.claim: A refusal direction computed locally for Qwen3.5-9B-Q4_K_M (hidden 4096) from a small harmful/benign prompt set yields a rank-1 LoRA that lowers its refusal rate by >50 points at <2 points of capability cost.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Refusal rate moves <10 points, or MMLU-style accuracy drops >2 points, or the LoRA loads but produces no measurable behavioural change.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Run the 9B fp16/GGUF with a small activation-capture harness on this box, take difference-in-means of last-token residual states on ~50 harmful vs ~50 benign prompts, unit-normalize, export A=r^T W / B=-r via the exporter's math against the Q4_K_M tensor names, then A/B the served model. If activation capture is too slow, first replicate the whole pipeline on the 1.7B Bonsai (463 MB, already local).
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: 0 USD; ESTIMATE 3-6 CPU/GPU-hours (9B forward passes dominate)

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The same runtime projection generalizes to a non-refusal behaviour: projecting out a mean-difference direction between long and short answers reduces mean output length by >30% at <2 points capability cost.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Mean output length moves <10%, or capability drops >2 points, or the direction is not separable (overlapping distributions).
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: On a tiny local model, collect residual activations for prompts whose reference answers are long vs short, compute the difference-in-means direction, build a rank-1 LoRA, sweep scale 0/1/2, and measure mean completion length and a short-answer accuracy set.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: llama-server with --lora-init-without-apply plus POST /lora-adapters changes the ablation scale per request with no reload, and refusal rate is monotonic in scale.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: The endpoint rejects the adapter or the scale, or the served outputs do not change between scale 0 and scale 2.
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Start the fork llama-server with --lora-init-without-apply on the 1.7B ternary model (small, local), POST scale 0/1/2 to /lora-adapters, and send the same prompt at each scale; diff outputs and record latency.

hypothesis_seeds.claim: The BF16-derived 5120-d direction transfers through Bonsai's quantization-aware training: at alpha 1 on the QAT pack the residual component along r falls below 1e-5.
hypothesis_seeds.falsifier: Residual fraction stays above 1e-4 (the selfcheck FAIL threshold) at alpha 1, or the ablation is mathematically exact but the behaviour does not move (direction captures the wrong feature).
hypothesis_seeds.cpu_experiment: Run scripts/selfcheck.py against the MLX pack on CPU (mlx-cpu) with a short prompt; compare before/after residual fractions at layers 0/20/38/63. Pair it with a behavioural A/B so a clean residual is not mistaken for a working direction.
hypothesis_seeds.est_cost: 0 USD; ESTIMATE 2-4 CPU-hours (minutes per forward pass, per the repo's own Dockerfile note)

open_questions: Does the BF16-estimated refusal direction actually capture the same behavioural feature in the QAT ternary pack? The repo states transfer through QAT has not been measured; only the residual-projection math is verified.
Does the rank-1 LoRA reproduce the README's PTQ1_0 behaviour change when served by the fork on this box? The README says only PTQ1_0 was run, no PQ2_0, and this box has no live 27B number yet.

Is the licence actually Apache-2.0? LICENSE holds only the 15-line short notice, GitHub reports NOASSERTION, and the README asserts Apache-2.0 'matching the underlying model' (the upstream pack is apache-2.0). The direction vector's provenance (derived from the base model) may carry its own terms.

Can a refusal or verbosity direction be computed 0-USD on CPU for the 9B (4096) and 35B-A3B (2048), which the 5120-d shipped direction cannot address, and does the lever survive Q4_K_M/Q3_K_M quantization (where a baked edit would NOT round away)?
How many tokens/seconds does the projection cost at scale 1 vs scale 0 in the fork, and does the two-extra-matmuls LoRA path measurably slow decode on an 8 GB card?
Does POST /lora-adapters on the fork's llama-server give genuinely per-request steering (concurrent requests at different scales) or is the scale global state?
Is the owner's 'qwen3.8 50b' a real model id? The Bonsai base is Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B (HF API 2026-09-20); no Qwen3.8-50B appeared in a 20-result HF search.

The town's dead-head/coherence-pruning thread is head pruning; this repo is whole-residual-stream direction ablation. Is there a shared mechanism (rank-1 projection) worth testing as a bridge, or are they orthogonal?
